name: Macher Jhol
subtitle: a thin turmeric and ginger fish broth built around fried rohu steaks

ingredients.qty: 600g rohu or katla, cut into 2cm cross-section steaks
ingredients.note: any firm freshwater fish on the bone

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave 15 minutes at room temperature.
Pat the steaks completely dry before they go in the oil, or they will stick and tear.
Mix the remaining turmeric, chilli powder, cumin powder and ginger with 4 tbsp water into a loose paste so it does not scorch in the pan.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then lower to medium-high.
Slide in the fish steaks and fry 3 minutes a side until the surface is firm and browned.
steps.tip: Do not move the fish for the first 3 minutes. It releases from the pan when it is ready.

steps.text: Lift the fish out onto a plate and leave the oil in the pan.
Fry the potato wedges in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden at the edges, then add the eggplant for 2 minutes.
Push the vegetables aside, add the nigella seeds to the clear space and let them pop for 10 seconds.
Stir in the spice paste and fry 2-3 minutes until it darkens and stops smelling raw.
steps.tip: If it sticks, add a tablespoon of water rather than more oil.

steps.text: Add the tomato, slit chillies, 700ml water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender.
Return the fish steaks, spooning gravy over them, and simmer 4 minutes only.
steps.tip: Overcooked fish goes cottony. Four minutes is enough — it finished cooking in the frying stage.

steps.text: Turn off the heat, scatter the coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 1 day refrigerated. Reheat gently just to a simmer; the fish toughens if it boils again.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
